Formulation
Predisposing: Occupational strain (nursing), recent travel to rural Vietnam.  
Precipitating: Febrile illness of one-week duration with night sweats, myalgia, nausea.  
Perpetuating: Ongoing symptoms causing reduced oral intake and work difficulties.  
Protective: Engagement with healthcare, willingness to attend urgent review.

Mental Health Care Plan Details
(Address each principal problem identified in Clinical Assessment)

Principal Problem: Acute febrile illness of unknown origin
- Patient Goal(s):
  • Identify cause of current illness and obtain effective treatment.  
  • Regain strength to return to work safely.
- Clinical Goal(s):
  • Exclude serious or exotic infection (e.g., malaria).  
  • Manage fever and dehydration; provide symptomatic relief.
- Actions (Patient):
  • Attend same-day clinic appointment in central London for physical examination and blood tests (including thick/thin films, inflammatory markers).  
  • Refrain from work until medically cleared.
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  • Arrange urgent clinic booking and document recommended investigations.  
  • Provide written summary for A&E if required.  
  • Review results and initiate appropriate treatment or referral (e.g., infectious diseases).

Secondary Problem: Chronic mechanical back pain
- Patient Goal(s):
  • Reduce pain; improve posture and daily function.
- Clinical Goal(s):
  • Continue physiotherapy program; monitor pain impact on work.
- Actions (Patient):
  • Adhere to prescribed physiotherapy exercises.  
  • Implement ergonomic strategies at work.
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  • Liaise with physiotherapist for progress updates.  
  • Consider analgesic review if pain persists.

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Need for urgent assessment; potential infectious causes; importance of blood testing; work exclusion until diagnosis confirmed.
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Persistent or rising fever, rigors, altered consciousness, rash, breathing difficulty.
- Coping Strategies: Adequate hydration, rest, antipyretics per advice, prompt presentation to emergency services if deterioration.
